title: What colour refinement and local views of the count table cannot see
claim: R0: the ladder of readings (a <= N1, W2 <= WL; B_r up to the full table, which determines the base). R1: every partial cube is a base (its betweenness solution set is its halfspaces). R2: F(a,b), two rings sharing a point, has k = max(a,b); for every count r, F(r,3r) and F(2r,2r) have equal views within count r and k = 3r against 2r, so no bounded-count reading determines k. R3: kappa(C10) and kappa(C5+C5) (simplex graphs, median, n = 21) agree under a, N1, W2 and 1-WL and have k = 2 against 3; B4 separates them, so local views and colour refinement are incomparable. R4 (classical): k cannot be computed from the table in polynomial time unless P = NP (Bandelt-van de Vel; via kappa and triangle-free 3-colouring); lambda is a matching. R5: distinct rows make W2 complete. R6: rings of arcs, split systems that are not bases, do the same.
standard_statement: Weisfeiler-Leman refinement and Hanf-Gaifman locality on split metrics of partial cubes; simplex graphs; tree number of median graphs.
prior_work: COUNT-BALLS-20261118-001 (reading a fails from n = 7); DISTANCE-ORDER-20261117-001 (the table determines these bases); REFINE-READ-20261107-001 (colour refinement on another object); classical: Weisfeiler-Leman, Cai-Furer-Immerman, Hanf, Gaifman, Djokovic-Winkler, Bandelt-van de Vel, Eppstein, Prowse-Woodall.
completion_gate: Ticket B's gates check R1 on four instances and R2, R3 on their smallest instances; the referee reviews the proofs.
